ext_name.description: Manifest name and the settings heading. The brand: keep "Tag Kit" as is and translate only "for". At most 75 characters (Chrome limit).

ext_short_name.description: Manifest short_name, where space is tight. The brand, kept as is. At most 12 characters (Chrome recommendation).

ext_description.message: Tags Steam games: AI Generated Content Disclosure, Anti-Cheat (kernel level first), 3rd-party DRM, account and EULA, and PvP.
ext_description.description: Manifest description and userscript @description. At most 132 characters (Chrome limit). Name each tag as Steam's own store in that language does.

ext_action_title.description: Tooltip of the extension's toolbar button, which opens the settings popup. At most 75 characters. Keep "Tag Kit for Steam" as in ext_name.

error_unexpected.description: Logged to the browser console when something fails without a more specific message. Short; developers read it, not players.

warn_breaker_opened.message: Steam refused or dropped a request; detection pauses for $seconds$ seconds ($breaker$).
warn_breaker_opened.description: Logged to the browser console when the extension stops asking Steam for a while after an error answer, to avoid being rate-limited. $breaker$ is an internal storage key such as v1:breaker; keep it as is.

notice_breaker_closed.description: Logged to the browser console when the pause after an error answer from Steam is over. $breaker$ is an internal storage key such as v1:breaker; keep it as is.

notice_page_disagrees.message: The store page says $page$ and Steam's data says $data$ for the $kind$ tag of app $app$.
notice_page_disagrees.description: Logged to the browser console in debug mode when the open game's page and the data Steam returns for it give different answers for one tag. $kind$ is the tag id and $page$ and $data$ are verdict states; keep them as they are.

kind_ai_heading.description: Steam's own heading of the block where a developer describes generative AI use. It titles the AI entry in the hover card, begins the screen reader name of the AI chip and heads the notice on the game's page. Use the wording Steam shows in this language.

kind_ai_chip.description: Short chip for a game whose developer filled in Steam's AI disclosure. Keep it to a few characters; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_kernel_heading.description: Steam's own line for a game whose anti-cheat runs at kernel level. It titles the entry in the hover card and begins the screen reader name of the chip. Use the wording Steam shows in this language.

kind_kernel_chip.description: Short chip for a game with kernel level anti-cheat. Keep it short; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_kernel_uninstall.message: Requires manual removal after game uninstall
kind_kernel_uninstall.description: Steam's own note in the hover card when a kernel level anti-cheat stays on the computer after the game is uninstalled.

kind_kernel_boot.message: Boot Protection - Requires both Secure Boot & TPM 2.0
kind_kernel_boot.description: Steam's own note in the hover card when the game needs boot protection. Use the wording Steam shows in this language; keep the hyphen between the two parts.

kind_anticheat_heading.description: Steam's own line for a game with anti-cheat software that does not run at kernel level. It titles the entry in the hover card and begins the screen reader name of the chip. Use the wording Steam shows in this language.

kind_anticheat_chip.description: Short chip for a game with anti-cheat software. Keep it short; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_drm_heading.description: Steam's own line for a game whose developer declared third-party DRM. It titles the entry in the hover card and begins the screen reader name of the chip; the DRM the developer named follows in the card, untranslated.

kind_drm_chip.description: Short chip for a game with third-party DRM. Keep it short; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_account_heading.description: Steam's own line for a game that needs an account with another company. It titles the entry in the hover card and begins the screen reader name of the chip; the account the developer named follows in the card, untranslated.

kind_account_chip.description: Short chip for a game that requires a third-party account. Keep it short; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_account_links.description: Steam's own note in the hover card, under the third-party account, when that account can be linked to the player's Steam account.

kind_eula_heading.description: Steam's own line for a game that makes the player accept an end user license agreement of another company. It titles the entry in the hover card and begins the screen reader name of the chip; the agreement names follow in the card, untranslated.

kind_eula_chip.description: Short chip for a game with a third-party end user license agreement. Use the abbreviation Steam uses in this language; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_pvp_heading.description: Title of the PvP entry in the hover card and start of the screen reader name of the chip. Use the abbreviation Steam uses in this language for player versus player.

kind_pvp_chip.description: Short chip for a game with a player versus player mode, as its Steam categories say. Use the abbreviation Steam uses in this language.

kind_pvp_category_pvp.description: Steam's category name for player versus player, listed in the hover card.

kind_pvp_category_online.description: Steam's category name for online player versus player, listed in the hover card.

kind_pvp_category_lan.description: Steam's category name for player versus player over a local network, listed in the hover card.

kind_pvp_category_split.description: Steam's category name for player versus player on one shared or split screen, listed in the hover card.

kind_iap_heading.description: Steam's category name for a game that sells items inside it. It titles the entry in the hover card and the banner, names the settings section and begins the screen reader name of the chip. Use the name Steam's store shows for this category in this language.

kind_iap_chip.description: Short chip for a game with in-app purchases, as its Steam categories say. Keep it short; it sits in a row and over game images.

kind_deck_heading.description: Steam's own heading of the Steam Deck rating Valve gives a game. It titles the entry in the hover card, names the settings section and, with the rating word, heads the entry in the notice on the game's page and the chip's screen reader name. Use the wording Steam shows in this language.

kind_deck_chip.description: Short device word at the start of a Steam Deck chip, followed by Steam's rating word (kind_facet_chip): "Deck Unsupported". Our short form of the device name, for chips only; keep it short.

kind_machine_heading.description: Steam's own heading of the Steam Machine rating Valve gives a game. It titles the entry in the hover card, names the settings section and, with the rating word, heads the entry in the notice on the game's page and the chip's screen reader name. Use the wording Steam shows in this language.

kind_machine_chip.description: Device word at the start of a Steam Machine chip, followed by Steam's rating word (kind_facet_chip): "Steam Machine Unsupported". The device name, which Steam has no short form for.

kind_compat_verified.description: Steam's word for the best Steam Deck and Steam Machine rating, shown under the heading in the hover card, after the device word on the chip and as a choice in the settings. Use the word Steam shows in this language.

kind_compat_playable.description: Steam's word for the middle Steam Deck and Steam Machine rating: the game works, with some effort. Shown like Verified. Use the word Steam shows in this language.

kind_compat_unsupported.description: Steam's word for a game Valve rated as not working on Steam Deck or Steam Machine. Shown like Verified. Use the word Steam shows in this language. Never use it for a game Valve has not rated.

kind_family_heading.description: Steam's own name of Family Sharing, the Steam feature that lets a family share a library. It titles the entry in the hover card, names the settings section, begins the screen reader name of the chip and is the choice for a game Steam lists it for. It is also the listed value's chip text, in full; the compact badge may cut it with an ellipsis when narrow. Use the word Steam shows in this language.

kind_family_unsupported.description: Steam's own words for a game that cannot be shared in a family library. The heading of the entry in the notice on the game's page, a choice in the settings, the package summary's name for the value and the screen reader name of its chip, for a paid game whose Steam feature list leaves Family Sharing out. Keep Steam's wording and capitalization in this language.

kind_family_unsupported_chip.description: Chip for a paid game whose Steam feature list leaves Family Sharing out. Our own short words, chosen by the maintainer; the chip's screen reader name gives Steam's words ("Family Sharing not Available"). Keep it short, it sits in a row and over game images; the compact badge may cut it with an ellipsis when narrow. Use this kind of wording only for this key and the hover card line of this value.

kind_family_unsupported_line.message: Family Sharing is not supported for this game
kind_family_unsupported_line.description: In the hover card, under the heading "Family Sharing", for a paid game whose Steam feature list leaves Family Sharing out. Our own sentence; the card always closes with the line that says it comes from the features Steam lists for the game. Keep it a plain statement and say nothing about why.

kind_chip_name.description: Screen reader name of a chip: the visible chip text, then Steam's full line for the kind. $chip$ is the chip text and $heading$ the full line.

kind_facet_chip.description: Visible text of a chip for a tag with values, such as "Deck Unsupported": the tag's short word, then Steam's word for the value. Keep the order natural in your language; add a colon if the two words would read as one phrase.

kind_facet_name.description: Steam's heading of a tag with values, then Steam's word for the value: the screen reader name of its chip, the heading of its entry in the notice on a game's page and its line in a package's summary.

kind_chip_more.description: Chip that stands for the kinds that do not fit beside the other chips. $count$ is how many kinds it stands for.

kind_chip_more_name.description: After the chip text, names the hidden chips for screen readers, as in "+2: more tags".

kind_full_game.description: In the hover card and in the notice on a demo's store page, right under a tag's heading when the tag is shown because the full game declared it; the demo did not declare it itself. "The full game" is the product the demo belongs to. Never say the demo declared it.

kind_full_game_valve.description: In the hover card and in the notice on a demo's store page, right under the heading of a fact Valve states (a Steam Deck or Steam Machine rating, Family Sharing) when it is shown because Valve states it for the full game; Valve says nothing about the demo itself. Never say the demo was rated or listed.

badge_card_declared.message: Declared by the developer on the store page
badge_card_declared.description: Last line of the hover card. It says the developer, not this extension, made the declarations above.

badge_card_valve.description: Last line of the hover card when it lists a fact Valve states, such as a Steam Deck rating. It says Valve, not this extension or the developer, is the source of those entries. With entries of both kinds it follows the line that names the developer.

kind_family_source.message: According to the features Steam lists for this game
kind_family_source.description: Last line of the hover card when it lists Family Sharing, instead of "According to Valve". It says the entry comes from the feature list Steam shows for the game, which Valve computes. With entries of other kinds it follows their source lines.

badge_card_service_label.message: AI service named by the developer:
badge_card_service_label.description: In that panel, precedes a product name inserted as data, untranslated.

badge_card_more.message: The full text is on the game's store page.
badge_card_more.description: In that panel, shown when it cuts a long developer text short.

badge_tags_title.message: Tag Kit tags for this product
badge_tags_title.description: Small label above the chips this extension adds to a game's own store page, right under Steam's "Popular user-defined tags for this product:" block, and above the Tag Kit summary at the top of a package page. It names the chips as ours, apart from the players' tags. Keep "Tag Kit" as is. No colon.

badge_summary_games_one.description: A line of the Tag Kit summary at the top of a package page, one per tag. $kind$ is Steam's own line for the tag, $count$ is how many of the package's games have a known answer for it and $tagged$ how many of those carry the tag. Neutral count words only: never say that the other games are free of it. Singular form, chosen by $count$.

badge_summary_games_other.description: A line of the Tag Kit summary at the top of a package page, one per tag. $kind$ is Steam's own line for the tag, $count$ is how many of the package's games have a known answer for it and $tagged$ how many of those carry the tag. Neutral count words only: never say that the other games are free of it. Plural form, chosen by $count$.

badge_summary_pending_one.description: A line at the end of the same summary while some of the package's games are still being looked up. $count$ is how many. Singular form.

badge_summary_pending_other.description: A line at the end of the same summary while some of the package's games are still being looked up. $count$ is how many. Plural form.

banner_source.description: In the notice on a game's store page, introduces the developer's text, which follows untranslated.

banner_region_label.description: Screen reader name of the notice on a game's page when it lists more than one kind, or only notes about ignored kinds, and every kind it lists comes from the developer.

banner_expand.description: Expands the collapsed text of the notice.

banner_collapse.description: Collapses the text of the notice again.

banner_ignore.description: Button on the notice that stops every tag and this notice for one game, in this extension only. The store has its own Ignore button; this one does not touch it.

banner_ignore_kind.description: Button on one kind's entry in the notice. It stops that kind's badge and entry for one game, in this extension only; the game's other tags stay.

banner_ignored.description: Replaces the notice after "Ignore this game".

banner_ignored_kind.description: Replaces one kind's entry in the notice after "Ignore for this tag". $heading$ is Steam's line for the kind.

banner_ignored_creator.description: Note on the notice, with an Undo button, once a developer or publisher is ignored for every tag. $name$ is the name Steam shows, untranslated, and $role$ is developer or publisher.

banner_ignored_creator_kind.description: Note on the notice, with an Undo button, once a developer or publisher is ignored for one tag. $name$ is the name Steam shows, untranslated, $role$ is developer or publisher and $heading$ is Steam's line for the tag.

notice_creator_stopped.description: Screen reader announcement after ignoring a developer or publisher for every tag. $name$ is the name Steam shows, untranslated, and $role$ is developer or publisher.

notice_creator_stopped_kind.message: Games by $name$ ($role$) will be ignored for $heading$
notice_creator_stopped_kind.description: Screen reader announcement after ignoring a developer or publisher for one tag. $name$ is the name Steam shows, untranslated, $role$ is developer or publisher and $heading$ is Steam's line for the tag.

notice_list_hidden_one.message: $count$ title has been hidden by Tag Kit based on your settings.
notice_list_hidden_one.description: A bar above search results, styled like Steam's own notice there, when a tag's list filter is set to Hide and it removed some results from this list. Worded like that notice ("2 titles have been excluded based on your preferences."); follow the words Steam uses for it in your language. $count$ is the number of results it hid. It names only the number: never which tags, and never that a game uses AI. Singular form.

notice_list_hidden_other.message: $count$ titles have been hidden by Tag Kit based on your settings.
notice_list_hidden_other.description: A bar above search results, styled like Steam's own notice there, when a tag's list filter is set to Hide and it removed some results from this list. Worded like that notice ("2 titles have been excluded based on your preferences."); follow the words Steam uses for it in your language. $count$ is the number of results it hid. It names only the number: never which tags, and never that a game uses AI. Plural form.

notice_list_revealed_one.description: Replaces notice_list_hidden after the person clicked notice_list_show: the same results show again, dimmed, on this page only. $count$ is the number of those results. Singular form.

notice_list_revealed_other.description: Replaces notice_list_hidden after the person clicked notice_list_show: the same results show again, dimmed, on this page only. $count$ is the number of those results. Plural form.

notice_list_show_one.description: Button after notice_list_hidden. Shows the hidden results on this page only; the settings stay as they are. "it" or "them" refers to the results. Singular form.

notice_list_show_other.description: Button after notice_list_hidden. Shows the hidden results on this page only; the settings stay as they are. "it" or "them" refers to the results. Plural form.

notice_list_hide_one.description: Button after notice_list_revealed. Hides those results again. Singular form.

notice_list_hide_other.description: Button after notice_list_revealed. Hides those results again. Plural form.

notice_marking_stopped.description: Screen reader announcement after "Ignore this game".

notice_marking_stopped_kind.message: This game will be ignored for $heading$
notice_marking_stopped_kind.description: Screen reader announcement after "Ignore for this tag". $heading$ is Steam's line for the tag.

notice_marking_restored.message: This game is no longer ignored
notice_marking_restored.description: Screen reader announcement after "Undo" or "Stop ignoring".

notice_marking_restored_kind.message: This game is no longer ignored for $heading$
notice_marking_restored_kind.description: Screen reader announcement after "Undo" or "Stop ignoring" for one tag. $heading$ is Steam's line for the tag.

notice_settings_saved.description: Screen reader announcement after a setting changes.

error_settings_save.message: Could not save this change. Try again.
error_settings_save.description: Under a setting whose change failed to save.

error_settings_load.message: Could not load your settings. Showing the defaults.
error_settings_load.description: Top of the settings page when stored settings cannot be read.

error_allow_list_save.message: Could not update this game. Try again.
error_allow_list_save.description: After "Ignore this game", "Undo" or "Stop ignoring" fails to save.

error_allow_list_load.message: Could not load the games you ignored. Try again later.
error_allow_list_load.description: Shown in the list of ignored games in the settings when the stored list cannot be read.

options_version.description: Under the product name at the top of the settings page and popup. $version$ is the release version, such as 2026.10.20; keep it as is.

options_badges.description: Switch label of one tag's badge.

options_badges_short.description: The same switch in the toolbar popup, where space is tight.

options_badges_help.message: Adds "$label$" to search and wishlist rows and to game images.
options_badges_help.description: Help under the badges switch. $label$ is the badge label.

options_banner.message: Entry in the banner on game pages
options_banner.description: Switch label of one tag's entry in the notice on a game's page.

options_banner_help.message: Shows this tag's entry above the purchase box.

options_filter_label.description: Label of a three-way choice: show, dim or hide these games in lists.

options_facets_label.description: Label of a group of checkboxes in a tag's settings, one per value Steam gives (Verified, Playable, Unsupported; Family Sharing, Family Sharing not Available). Only the ticked values get the tag.

options_facets_help.message: Badges, banner entries and the list filter act on the values ticked here. With none ticked, the tag marks no game.

options_filter_off.description: Leave these games as they are.

options_filter_off_help.message: Lists stay as they are, apart from badges.

options_filter_dim_help.message: Fades these games in lists. Hover to see one clearly.

options_filter_hide_help.message: Removes these games from lists. Where hiding would break a list, they are dimmed instead.

options_color_label.description: Label of a text field where the person types a hex color for one tag, and the title of the color help in the General tab. It colors the tag's badge, its entry in the banner and its hover card, so use the same word as the badge switch. "(experimental)" marks the setting as unfinished; keep it in the label.

options_color_placeholder.description: Shown inside the empty color field: no custom color is set, so the tag keeps the extension's default violet. One word.

options_color_help.message: Type a hex code such as #8f73f3, with or without the #, in a tag's tab. It colors that tag's badge, its entry in the banner and its card. Contrast is not checked, so a very light or very dark color can be hard to read. Leave it empty for the default violet.
options_color_help.description: Help on colors, once in the General settings tab under the color title. Keep the example code as it is. It must say that contrast is not checked.

options_color_invalid.message: Not a color. Type three or six hex digits, such as #8f73f3.
options_color_invalid.description: Error under the color field while the text is not a hex color. Keep the example code as it is.

options_color_reset.description: Button that clears a tag's custom color and goes back to the default violet. One word.

options_color_reset_label.description: Screen reader name of the Reset button next to a color field. Starts with the button's visible word. $heading$ is Steam's own line for the tag.

options_language_auto.description: First entry of the language picker.

options_language_help.message: Automatic follows the store page's language when a translation exists, and English otherwise.

options_section_allow.description: Caption of the games in a card of ignored items, and the name of that list in a backup.

options_allow_since.description: Under a game you ignored. $date$ is already formatted for the locale.

options_allow_scope_all.description: Heading of the games ignored for every tag, in the list of ignored games. The games ignored for one tag sit under Steam's line for that tag.

options_allow_restore.description: Button next to a game you ignored.

options_allow_restore_label.description: Screen reader name of the "Stop ignoring" button; $name$ is the game's name, untranslated, and $scope$ names the tag it was ignored for, or all tags.

options_allow_empty.message: None yet. Use "$action$" on a game page.
options_allow_empty.description: Shown in a card of ignored items when it lists nothing. $action$ is the label of the button that ignores: "Ignore this game" for all tags, "Ignore for this tag" for one tag.

options_section_allow_developers.description: Caption of the developers in a card of ignored items, and the name of that list in a backup.

options_section_allow_publishers.description: Caption of the publishers in a card of ignored items, and the name of that list in a backup.

error_creator_list_save.message: Could not update this developer or publisher. Try again.
error_creator_list_save.description: After "Stop ignoring" on a developer or publisher, or its ignore button on a game page, fails to save.

error_creator_list_load.message: Could not load the developers and publishers you ignored. Try again later.
error_creator_list_load.description: Shown in the lists of ignored developers and publishers in the settings when a stored list cannot be read.

banner_role_developer.description: A game's developer as a role label: a row in the notice that ignores a developer or publisher, and in parentheses after the name in sentences about it.

banner_role_publisher.description: A game's publisher as a role label: a row in the notice that ignores a developer or publisher, and in parentheses after the name in sentences about it.

notice_creator_restored.description: Screen reader announcement after "Undo" or "Stop ignoring" on a developer or publisher. $name$ is the name Steam shows, untranslated, and $role$ is developer or publisher.

notice_creator_restored_kind.description: Screen reader announcement after "Undo" or "Stop ignoring" on a developer or publisher for one tag. $name$ is the name Steam shows, untranslated, $role$ is developer or publisher and $heading$ is Steam's line for the tag.

banner_creators_toggle.description: Label of the closed section at the foot of the notice that lists the game's developers and publishers, each with buttons that ignore it in this extension only. The settings name it when the list of ignored developers or publishers is empty.

banner_ignore_creator_kind.description: Button in the closed section of the notice that ignores one developer or publisher for one tag, in this extension only. $chip$ is the tag's short label. A screen reader adds the name and role of the developer or publisher after it.

banner_ignore_creator_all.description: Button in the closed section of the notice that ignores one developer or publisher for every tag, in this extension only. A screen reader adds the name and role of the developer or publisher after it.

options_section_backup.description: Title of the settings card that saves the settings and ignore lists to a file and restores them. Full options page and userscript dialog only.

options_backup_help.message: Save your settings and ignore lists to a file on this device, or restore them from one. The extension and the userscript read the same file. Lookup results are not included.
options_backup_help.description: Help under the Backup title. The file stays on the person's device; nothing is sent anywhere. "userscript" is the script version of the product. "Lookup results" are the cached answers about games, which are not in the file.

options_backup_download.description: Button that saves the settings and ignore lists to a JSON file through the browser's download.

options_backup_restore.description: Button that opens the file chooser to pick a backup file. Nothing changes until the person confirms with options_backup_confirm. Also the accessible name of the file chooser.

options_backup_summary_title.description: Title of the check shown after a valid backup file is picked, before anything changes. $date$ is the day the backup was made, formatted for the language.

options_backup_summary_list.description: One line of the check after a backup file is picked: a list in the file and how many entries it holds. $list$ is a settings card title such as "Games you ignored", $number$ a number.

options_backup_summary_skipped_one.message: $count$ entry cannot be read and will be left out
options_backup_summary_skipped_one.description: Line of the check after a backup file is picked, when some ignore list entries in it are damaged. $count$ is how many. Singular form.

options_backup_summary_skipped_other.message: $count$ entries cannot be read and will be left out
options_backup_summary_skipped_other.description: Line of the check after a backup file is picked, when some ignore list entries in it are damaged. $count$ is how many. Plural form.

options_backup_restore_note.message: Restore replaces the settings here with the ones in the file and adds its ignored items to your lists. Nothing you ignored here is removed.
options_backup_restore_note.description: Note in the check before the person confirms a restore: what the restore will do.

options_backup_confirm.description: Primary button of the check: applies the picked backup file.

options_backup_cancel.description: Button of the check: closes it and changes nothing.

notice_backup_downloaded.description: Status line and screen reader announcement after the backup file was handed to the browser's download.

notice_backup_restored_one.message: Backup restored. $count$ new entry was added to your ignore lists.
notice_backup_restored_one.description: Status line and screen reader announcement after a restore. $count$ is how many ignore list entries were not on this browser before. Singular form.

notice_backup_restored_other.message: Backup restored. $count$ new entries were added to your ignore lists.
notice_backup_restored_other.description: Status line and screen reader announcement after a restore. $count$ is how many ignore list entries were not on this browser before. Plural form.

notice_backup_skipped_one.message: $count$ entry could not be read and was left out.
notice_backup_skipped_one.description: Follows notice_backup_restored when some ignore list entries in the file were damaged. $count$ is how many. Singular form.

notice_backup_skipped_other.message: $count$ entries could not be read and were left out.
notice_backup_skipped_other.description: Follows notice_backup_restored when some ignore list entries in the file were damaged. $count$ is how many. Plural form.

error_backup_invalid.message: $name$ is not a Tag Kit backup, or is too large to be one. Nothing was changed.
error_backup_invalid.description: Error after picking a file that is not a backup of this product. $name$ is the file name, shown as is. "Tag Kit" is the brand, kept as is.

error_backup_newer.message: $name$ comes from a newer version of Tag Kit. Update Tag Kit here, then try again. Nothing was changed.
error_backup_newer.description: Error after picking a backup made by a later version of the product. $name$ is the file name, shown as is. "Tag Kit" is the brand, kept as is.

error_backup_read.message: $name$ could not be read. Nothing was changed.
error_backup_read.description: Error when the browser cannot read the picked file. $name$ is the file name, shown as is.

error_backup_create.message: The backup could not be made. Try again.
error_backup_create.description: Error when "Download backup" fails because the settings or lists cannot be read or the browser refuses the download.

error_backup_restore.message: The backup could not be fully restored. Try again; restoring the same file twice is safe.
error_backup_restore.description: Error when saving a restore fails. A retry only adds what is missing, so it is safe.

options_privacy_no_reports.message: Sends no reports. It only reads what developers report on Steam.
options_privacy_no_reports.description: Privacy bullet: the product never sends reports about games or users anywhere; it only shows what developers reported to Steam.

options_privacy_storage.message: Settings and results stay in this browser.

options_privacy_lookup.message: To check a game, it asks Valve's own store servers, without your cookies or account.

options_privacy_nothing_sent.message: Nothing is sent to us or anyone else. No analytics.

options_unaffiliated.message: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve Corporation. Steam is a trademark of Valve Corporation.
options_unaffiliated.description: Legal line at the bottom of the settings; keep the names as they are.

options_unaffiliated_short.message: Not affiliated with Valve. Nothing leaves your browser except lookups to Valve's store.

options_all_settings.description: Screen reader name and tooltip of the gear button at the top of the toolbar popup, which opens the full settings page in a tab.

options_kind_enabled.description: Master switch of one tag in the settings. Its section is titled with Steam's line for the tag.

options_kind_enabled_help.message: Off removes its badges, its entry in the banner and its list filter.
options_kind_enabled_help.description: Help under the master switch of one tag.

options_state_on.description: Short status on a tag's settings tab, after its name: the tag is switched on. It describes the tag's master switch, not any game.

options_state_off.description: Short status on a tag's settings tab, after its name: the tag is switched off. It describes the tag's master switch, not any game.

options_tabs_label.description: Screen reader name of the row of tabs at the top of the settings: General, then one tab per tag.

options_tab_general.description: The first settings tab and its heading: language, colors, what is ignored for all tags, backup and privacy. One word if the language allows.

options_allow_kind_title.description: Title of the card in a tag's settings tab that lists the games, developers and publishers ignored for that tag only.

options_allow_all_title.description: Title of the card in the General tab that lists the games, developers and publishers ignored for every tag.

options_allow_all_note_one.message: $count$ item ignored for all tags also applies here.
options_allow_all_note_one.description: Note in a tag's settings tab, under what is ignored for that tag: how many games, developers and publishers are ignored for every tag, which this tag follows too. $count$ is how many. Singular form.

options_allow_all_note_other.message: $count$ items ignored for all tags also apply here.
options_allow_all_note_other.description: The same note, plural form. $count$ is how many.

options_allow_all_show.description: Button after that note that opens the General tab at the list of what is ignored for all tags. "General" is the tab's name (options_tab_general).

options_color_help_short.message: Contrast is not checked. See General.
options_color_help_short.description: Short help under a tag's color field. The full help is in the General tab (options_tab_general), which this names. It must say that contrast is not checked.

userscript_menu_settings.description: Entry in the script manager's menu (Tampermonkey, Violentmonkey) that opens the settings dialog on a store page. One word.

userscript_close.description: Button that closes the userscript settings dialog.

userscript_reload_note.message: Changes apply on the next page load.
userscript_reload_note.description: Shown under the settings in the userscript dialog when the script manager cannot apply a change to other open store tabs at once.
